Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver

Class DesktopMode

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.DesktopMode
public final class DesktopMode extends Object
Decides whether the desktop starts as the 3D scene-graph desktop or as the conventional-Swing 2D desktop (org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d).

The decision is driven by the lg.fws.mode system property and by a capability probe:

  • lg.fws.mode=2d - force the MDI 2D desktop (applications in internal frames inside the desktop window; manual opt-in, no prompt).
  • lg.fws.mode=swing - force the conventional Swing desktop (DesktopSwing: the same MDI shell as 2d - applications in internal frames inside the desktop's JDesktopPane - under the Metal look and feel; manual opt-in, no prompt).
  • lg.fws.mode=3d - force the 3D desktop and fail loudly if 3D is unavailable (the pre-2D-mode behaviour).
  • any other value (dev, x11, unset) - start 3D when the probe says it can work, otherwise fall back to the MDI 2D desktop after asking the user to confirm.

The two probe steps mirror what boot needs: that Java 3D is on the classpath and recent enough (the pickfast package, present since the 1.5 build 2 release the desktop has always required), and that a graphics configuration able to render 3D exists on this display. Both are queried reflectively so that this class - and Main, which loads it before any 3D class - stays loadable on a JVM with no Java 3D at all.

    • probe

      public static DesktopMode.Capability probe()
      Probes this JVM/display for 3D support. Never throws: any failure is reported as an unavailable capability with a reason.

    • resolve

      public static DesktopMode.Mode resolve(String modeProperty, boolean java3dPresent, boolean glInitOk)
      Resolves the desktop to start from the mode property and a probe result.
      Parameters:
      modeProperty - the raw lg.fws.mode value (may be null)
      java3dPresent - a new-enough Java 3D is on the classpath
      glInitOk - a 3D-capable graphics configuration was found
